facts.statement: Wellnhoferia had a shorter tail and a shorter fourth toe compared to Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: While Wellnhoferia was similar to Archaeopteryx, it had a shorter tail and its fourth toe was shorter than that of Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Andrzej Elżanowski described Wellnhoferia in 2001, attributing its differences from Archaeopteryx to phylogenetic reduction rather than individual variation.
facts.quote: Andrzej Elżanowski (2001) of the Institute of Zoology of the University of Wrocław, Poland, determined the differences resulted from a "phylogenetic reduction rather than individual variation."

facts.statement: The type specimen for Wellnhoferia is the Solnhofen Specimen of Archaeopteryx (BSP 1999).
facts.quote: The type specimen is the Solnhofen Specimen of Archaeopteryx (BSP 1999).

facts.statement: The specimen was discovered in the 1960s near Eichstätt, Germany, described in 1988 by Peter Wellnhofer, and is now housed in the Bürgermeister-Müller-Museum in Solnhofen.
facts.quote: Discovered in the 1960s near Eichstätt, Germany and described in 1988 by Wellnhofer (as a specimen of Archaeopteryx), it is now in the Bürgermeister-Müller-Museum in Solnhofen.

facts.statement: The specimen was originally classified as a Compsognathus by an amateur collector.
facts.quote: It was originally classified as a Compsognathus by an amateur collector.

facts.statement: A 2007 study by Mayr et al. concluded that Wellnhoferia is actually a specimen of Archaeopteryx lithographica, contradicting Elżanowski's original classification.
facts.quote: Although Elżanowski found significant differences between Wellnhoferia and Archaeopteryx, a 2007 study by Mayr et al. found Wellnhoferia was a specimen of Archaeopteryx lithographica.

facts.statement: Senter and Robins (2003) supported Elżanowski's decision to name Wellnhoferia a new genus.
facts.quote: Senter and Robins (2003), however, supported Elżanowski's naming of a new genus.

facts.statement: Wellnhoferia belongs to the order Archaeopterygiformes.
Wellnhoferia belongs to the family Archaeopterygidae.
The genus Wellnhoferia was established by Elżanowski in 2001.
The type species of the genus is W. grandis, described by Elżanowski in 2001.
Wellnhoferia is an extinct genus of a primitive avialan closely related to Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Wellnhoferia es un género extinto de un avialano primitivo cercanamente relacionada con Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Elżanowski created the new genus Wellnhoferia after finding significant differences between the Solnhofen specimen and Archaeopteryx, naming it after Peter Wellnhofer.
facts.quote: Elżanowski halló diferencias significativas entre el espécimen de Solnhofen y Archaeopteryx y creó un nuevo género, Wellnhoferia, dedicándoselo a Wellnhofer.

facts.statement: The parent group for Wellnhoferia is Avialae.
